verdict: HOLD: remediation is not complete and this is not release sign-off

findings.title: Mod export success still does not prove bytes were written
findings.kind: Confirmed in the newly packaged RF mod source; no game fault injection
findings.detail: The copy wrapper discards copyFile's result and accepts a nonthrowing call plus an existing destination. Move recovery can then delete the source. Atomic/direct/mirror write paths do not consistently check write and close outcomes; saveFile fallback equates pcall success with persisted success.
findings.impact: Disk, permission or nonthrowing I/O failures can leave stale or damaged exports while success bookkeeping advances. This finding concerns the packaged code; it does not claim the current save has been damaged.
findings.fix: Use one explicit persistence result contract for copy/write/close/save/mirror paths. Preserve the previous good export and recoverable temporary bytes until replacement is confirmed.
accept: Inject false/nil-plus-error write, close and copy results with an existing destination.
The previous export remains usable, temporary recovery data is retained and no success/mirror notification occurs on failure.
A subsequent successful retry recovers; verify in the supported game runtime as well as isolated fixtures.

findings.title: Opaque browser origins still inherit native loopback trust
findings.kind: Reproduced in isolated candidate-code fixtures
findings.detail: `getRequestOrigin` turns explicit Origin: null and malformed origins into an empty string. Both the write guard and WebSocket origin guard then take the no-origin local-client branch. The fixture accepted both, while rejecting an ordinary hostile HTTPS origin.
findings.impact: A browser-origin boundary can be bypassed on locally reachable privileged HTTP/WS paths. This is a boundary reproduction, not a live browser exploit against your machine.
findings.fix: Preserve absent, opaque, malformed and valid origins as different states. Reject opaque/malformed browser origins before any locality exemption; share the policy between HTTP and WS.
accept: Origin: null and malformed Origin are rejected for every privileged HTTP route and WS upgrade.
An actually absent Origin follows an explicit native-client policy, without allowing browser cases to masquerade as native.
Exercise the full Express middleware chain and a sandboxed browser origin against an isolated profile.

findings.title: FTP detail filenames can escape the intended cache
findings.kind: Reproduced in an isolated Windows-path fixture
findings.detail: `syncFtpDetailsCache` only checks that a remote entry starts with animals_ and ends with .json. Backslashes and traversal components survive into path.join. A mocked listing directed the download to C:\audit\outside.json instead of the userData subtree.
findings.impact: A malicious or compromised configured FTP source can influence a local write destination outside the cache. No real files were created or overwritten by the fixture.
findings.fix: Accept only the supported pen-filename grammar, reject separators/drive syntax/dot traversal, and validate the resolved destination against the exact details root before any unlink, download or rename.
accept: Reject Windows and POSIX traversal, absolute paths, UNC/drive forms, alternate-data-stream syntax and unsupported pen names.
Assert the exact expected destination for legitimate integer and composite pen filenames.
Run the same hostile listing through bulk sync and per-pen download paths with a fake filesystem.

findings.title: Failed FTP replacement deletes the last good cache first
findings.kind: Reproduced in an isolated filesystem fixture
findings.detail: `safeDownload` unlinks localFinal before attempting rename. With a simulated EACCES at rename, it returned false with the final file absent and only the temporary file remaining. Per-pen FTP replacement contains the same unlink-before-rename sequence.
findings.impact: A transient replacement failure removes the last usable local snapshot and degrades offline/recovery behavior. This is local cache loss, not demonstrated game-save corruption.
findings.fix: Introduce a last-good-preserving replacement primitive with explicit failure cleanup and recovery. Apply it to main Lua/XML downloads and per-pen cache replacement.
accept: Simulate rename denial after a successful download and assert the original final bytes still exist.
Exercise retry, process interruption and replacement of an existing target on Windows.
Do not accept a download merely because it is nonempty; validate its expected document before making it current.

findings.title: Sampled animal count correction still changes averages
findings.kind: Packaged-mod source confirmation
findings.detail: Sampled buckets scale count and weighted sums together, then correct count alone to meet the reported population. Later averages divide unchanged sums by corrected counts. The inspected average helper also drops nonpositive sums, so measured all-zero health does not become an explicit aggregate zero.
findings.impact: Herd average health, weight, age and genetics can change solely because head counts were reconciled; unknown and measured zero remain conflated at the aggregate boundary.
findings.fix: Retain sample means and sample sizes separately from estimated population counts; preserve measured zero with an explicit known/unknown state.
accept: Changing an estimated bucket population does not change its measured sample mean.
Weighted farm means use the declared weighting basis.
All-zero measured health remains known zero, not omitted or healthy-by-default.

findings.title: Courseplay finance still falls back to purchase price
findings.kind: Packaged-mod source confirmation
findings.detail: The incremental-fleet finance branch reads row.sellValue, row.sellPrice or row.price. The inspected vehicle serializer writes purchase price into row.price and the shown sell-value path stores it under ads.sellValue.
findings.impact: Vehicle asset value and net worth can be inflated on this collection path.
findings.fix: Export a canonical top-level valuation with a valuation basis and use it consistently in finance and vehicle views. Do not silently substitute purchase cost for resale value.
accept: A vehicle with purchase 100000 and sell value 40000 contributes the declared resale value on both collector paths.
Zero sell value remains valid; missing value remains explicitly unknown.
ADS absence and Courseplay on/off do not silently change valuation meaning.

findings.title: Courseplay compatibility still traverses the fleet twice per update
findings.kind: Packaged-mod source confirmation; no FPS benchmark
findings.detail: FarmDashboard:update calls the compatibility tick. When Courseplay is loaded, shieldFleetIfNeeded performs two complete fleet passes on each tick, without the no-Courseplay pending-work gate.
findings.impact: Steady-state frame work grows with fleet size even when no shop/vehicle transition needs repair. The audit did not measure an FPS loss.
findings.fix: Retain the required two-phase ordering for pending transitions, but process a bounded dirty set or incremental cursor instead of every vehicle every update.
accept: A stable 400-vehicle fleet does not require 800 guard iterations every update.
Shop spawn and multiplayer join cases retain correct ordering and stream behavior.
Capture per-slice duration and iteration counts on small and large saves before/after.

findings.title: Adaptive cadence still uses a requested interval that setters do not update
findings.kind: Packaged-mod source confirmation
findings.detail: _userCollectionCycleMs is captured during config load and preferred by adaptive cadence. The inspected synced-settings and setInt paths update config.collectionCycleMs but not that requested-value field.
findings.impact: The user's interval choice can be overwritten or ignored by the next adaptive adjustment.
findings.fix: Use one authoritative requested cadence and compute effective cadence separately. Route local, synced and persisted changes through the same setter.
accept: Changing cadence through each supported settings path changes requested cadence.
Adaptive scaling may slow collection for load but does not forget the user's request.
Save/reload preserves both intent and documented effective behavior.

findings.title: Collector failure still collapses into an empty payload
findings.kind: Packaged-mod source confirmation; full scheduler fault injection outstanding
findings.detail: `safeCollect` returns an empty table both for missing/failed collection and for empty results, without an error status. Legacy collection consumes that result, and other completion paths still update cached data/finish slices without a uniform failure envelope.
findings.impact: Downstream code cannot reliably distinguish a successful empty section from a failed collection; stale/clear/freshness decisions remain fragile.
findings.fix: Return an explicit collected/empty/failed result with generation and diagnostic state, and propagate it through incremental and legacy scheduling without marking failures fresh.
accept: Force each supported collector to throw or return an explicit failure.
Keep the last good value labelled stale, do not fabricate a successful empty collection, and do not advance a successful cycle marker.
Request servicing remains responsive during sustained collector failure.

findings.title: Station-name rules still fabricate sell offers
findings.kind: Packaged-mod source confirmation
findings.detail: Although synthetic whole stations were removed, Method 8 still inserts products and fixed multipliers into existing named stations, including Grain Mill and Biogas Plant. Those prices feed the crop min/max/best-location calculation.
findings.impact: The dashboard can recommend an offer that was inferred from a station name rather than observed from the game.
findings.fix: Export real supported station/fill-type offers only. If estimates are useful, keep them explicitly labelled and out of authoritative best-price calculations.
accept: A real station with a familiar name but no matching fill-type offer gains no fabricated offer.
Best location is based only on observed comparable prices.
Localized/custom station names do not control price validity.

findings.title: Bale enumeration still budgets accepted rows rather than examined entries
findings.kind: Packaged-mod source confirmation
findings.detail: The iterator restarts pairs over a source table, skips previously seen entries, and increments its cap primarily for newly accepted entries. A large table of non-bale or already-seen objects can therefore require a broad scan in one slice.
findings.impact: The nominal row budget does not bound actual work and can still cause long game-thread slices.
findings.fix: Retain a stable enumeration cursor and charge the budget for every inspected entry, including rejected and duplicate objects.
accept: A source with many non-bales stops after the configured examined-entry/time budget.
Large repeated scans do not restart through all previously seen objects.
Mutation between slices does not duplicate/lose accepted bales or trap the cursor.

findings.title: FTP intervals can overlap and stale downloads can still commit files
findings.kind: Candidate-source confirmation of the overlapping FTP branch
findings.detail: The interval starts another batch without awaiting the previous batch. Poll generation checks occur before safeDownload and after it, but safeDownload replaces the final file internally before the post-download generation check. Generation-specific temporary names do not prevent an older operation from committing the shared final file.
findings.impact: Slow connections or configuration changes can create duplicate work and replace current disk data with an obsolete operation, even if renderer ingestion is later skipped.
findings.fix: Use one in-flight operation per server/context, cancel superseded transfers, and check generation immediately before committing bytes. Carry that identity through XML/detail work and teardown.
accept: Delay an old transfer across a newer completed poll: old bytes never become final.
Configuration changes and shutdown cancel pending work and leave no active timers/watchers.
Instrument concurrency and verify no overlapping work per server under sustained slow feeds.

findings.title: The HTTP total deadline still behaves as an idle timeout
findings.kind: Reproduced with candidate code and a simulated trickle response
findings.detail: The 45-second deadline is checked when entering a request/redirect, but there is no independent wall-clock cancellation timer for an active body. A mocked stream was still pending at 60 seconds and then returned HTTP 200. Response aborted/error settlement also remains incomplete in the inspected function.
findings.impact: A slowly streaming or prematurely aborted feed can keep collection work pending beyond the advertised deadline and amplify polling overlap.
findings.fix: Use an absolute timer and one settle/cleanup path across redirects, request errors, response errors, aborts and body completion.
accept: Continuous small chunks cannot exceed the total request budget.
Aborted and errored response bodies settle exactly once and remove listeners/timers.
A late response cannot mutate a superseded poll generation.

findings.title: FTP pen freshness still trusts client mtime and a missing dirty index
findings.kind: Candidate-source confirmation
findings.detail: Bulk detail sync compares remote mtime with the downloaded file's local mtime. Per-pen detail re-fetches only when dirtyAt is positive and newer than the local timestamp; a cached file with a missing index can therefore be reused indefinitely.
findings.impact: Clock skew and missing/stale indexes can leave animal detail old even while the overview continues updating.
findings.fix: Persist remote generation identity separately from local receipt time and apply a bounded revalidation policy when an index is absent or unreliable.
accept: Equal-sized remote updates are detected across host/client clock skew.
A missing index cannot suppress revalidation indefinitely.
Display age/source and distinguish cache fallback from confirmed current detail.

findings.title: Unstamped export freshness is still renewed after restart
findings.kind: Candidate-source confirmation of the accepted unstamped-export path
findings.detail: The content hash excludes weather and is not included in the persisted cache identity. On new in-memory state, the same unstamped export receives a new receipt-based lastLuaReceivedAt.
findings.impact: Old cached data can appear fresh after a restart; an unstamped weather-only update can also be missed by freshness detection. This is a legacy/unstamped-input path, not a claim that every current export lacks a timestamp.
findings.fix: Persist accepted source identity and production age. Keep transport receipt separate from generation time and cover every supported section in the identity contract.
accept: Restarting with identical unstamped bytes does not make them newly live.
A genuinely new generation is recognized even when numeric farm values are unchanged.
Weather-only changes and malformed timestamps have explicit, tested behavior.

findings.title: Hold and snapshot logic still retains legitimately cleared sections
findings.kind: Candidate-source confirmation
findings.detail: Backup updates remember nonempty animals without clearing the prior backup on an authoritative empty result. Snapshot forwarding restores previous animals/stock when the next section is empty; stock and RF hold branches still conflate empty with unavailable.
findings.impact: Removed animals, exhausted stock or disabled optional data can reappear during fallback/restart, undermining confidence in the dashboard.
findings.fix: Represent collected-empty, omitted, failed and disabled states explicitly. Carry generation-scoped clears through in-memory hold, persisted snapshots and restart hydration.
accept: A valid empty collection remains empty through subsequent omission and restart.
Disabled optional mods do not reappear from old snapshots.
Failed collection may retain a labelled last-known value, never silently convert a clear into stale content.

findings.title: Detail generations are still dropped and zero pens can receive old animals
findings.kind: Reproduced in isolated candidate-helper fixtures
findings.detail: `makeCacheEntry` still drops generatedAt. A husbandry reporting zero animals accepted two retained detail rows and was marked hydrated. The newer code prefers some smaller unique-ID lists, but does not establish generation correctness or a zero-population tombstone.
findings.impact: Sold or removed animals can reappear as detail rows, and choosing the newest complete pen snapshot remains unreliable.
findings.fix: Carry generation through cache construction, choose detail by validated identity/generation rather than row count, and treat an authoritative zero population as a clear that rejects prior detail.
accept: generatedAt survives load/cache/selection round trips.
A zero-head pen produces zero detail rows despite an old file on disk.
A newer smaller herd wins over an older larger one, independent of filename ordering.

findings.title: Ambiguous fleet ownership is still promoted from farm heuristics
findings.kind: Candidate-source confirmation
findings.detail: The transient-pool resolver scores farms using livestock, land, current fleet and ADS presence, then writes the selected farm into ownerFarmId/farmId when the fallback applies.
findings.impact: An ambiguous ownership guess can become authoritative-looking fleet and financial data on the wrong farm.
findings.fix: Prefer explicit stable-ID ownership. Preserve unknown/ambiguous ownership and provenance rather than manufacturing an owner from farm characteristics.
accept: Two plausible farms do not cause arbitrary reassignment.
Any fallback is labelled and excluded from authoritative farm totals until confirmed.
Stable-ID and saved ownership cases continue to resolve without relying on scoring.

findings.title: One XML vehicle can still be consumed through two matching indices
findings.kind: Reproduced using the candidate matching branches
findings.detail: A configuration-key match removes a row from one list but leaves its UID index available. The fixture matched the same XML object first by configuration and then again by UID.
findings.impact: Distinct live vehicles can inherit the same saved identity, ownership or values, producing duplicate or misleading fleet information.
findings.fix: Use one consumed-record set and one removal operation across UID, farm/config and generic-config indices. Reserve authoritative UID matches before ambiguous fallback matching.
accept: A configuration match followed by a UID match cannot consume the same XML record twice.
Repeated models on multiple farms retain their distinct identities.
Order permutations produce stable one-to-one matches.

findings.title: Field IDs and farmland IDs still share a collision-prone seen set
findings.kind: Candidate-source confirmation of one remaining branch
findings.detail: The Lua-only append branch checks seenKeys against both field.id and farmlandId even though XML keys use farmlandId-or-id. A valid field can be suppressed because its field ID happens to equal a different record's farmland ID. The separate prior ownership-precedence branch was not fully re-executed here.
findings.impact: Valid fields may disappear from merged output when identifier domains collide.
findings.fix: Keep field identity and farmland ownership identity in separate indices and deduplicate only with an explicit matching contract.
accept: A field ID equal to another parcel's farmland ID does not remove either valid record.
One farmland containing multiple fields is handled intentionally.
Repeat the earlier owner-transfer/owner-zero fixtures before closing the broader prior finding.

findings.title: XML change detection still misses changes below the maximum mtime
findings.kind: Reproduced with a synthetic per-file stat fixture
findings.detail: The fingerprint remains maximum mtime plus total size. Changing one file's mtime from 1000 to 2000 while another remained 9999 produced the same fingerprint, 9999:200.
findings.impact: A valid XML update can be skipped and old field/vehicle/economy data retained until another fingerprint component changes.
findings.fix: Fingerprint a stable per-file tuple of identity, size and modification time, with content/generation checks where metadata collisions are possible.
accept: A same-size change to any individual file invalidates the collection.
Deletion, addition and replacement are detected independently of the newest other file.
Retain parse avoidance for truly unchanged input.

findings.title: The Lua syntax gate still cannot start
findings.kind: Reproduced by the requested validation command
findings.detail: `node tools/check-lua-syntax.mjs` exits with MODULE_NOT_FOUND for luaparse. No Lua files were parsed by this attempted gate.
findings.impact: The packaged mod has no successful current syntax-gate evidence from the declared command. JavaScript tests do not replace this.
findings.fix: Make the parser a reproducible declared development dependency or select an explicitly supported installed runtime. Keep syntax failure nonzero and include the check in release validation.
accept: A clean dependency installation can execute the checker without global packages.
All intended Lua files are enumerated and parsed; the report states the actual count.
A deliberately invalid temporary fixture makes the gate fail.

findings.title: Integration cases still pass without exercising their assertions
findings.kind: Observed in the current Jest output
findings.detail: The transient-pool integration case returned early when the expected remapped vehicle was absent. The live Giants HTTP-feed case returned early unless its opt-in environment was set. Jest counted both as passes.
findings.impact: Green totals overstate integration coverage, including a path whose missing result should be a regression rather than a pass.
findings.fix: Separate deterministic fixture tests from opt-in live tests. Make missing required fixture records fail, and report unavailable live cases as actual skips with reasons.
accept: Removing the expected ownership output fails a deterministic test.
Disabled live integration is listed as skipped, not passed.
Release evidence distinguishes unit, synthetic integration and real dedicated-server coverage.

findings.title: Transport-only settings changes still do not refresh the live poller
findings.kind: Reproduced in configuration fixtures; retained poller object confirmed in candidate source
findings.detail: The server signature includes connection identity and secret revisions but omits ftpSecure and httpFeedSecure. Changing only either flag returns no reboot. The FTP coordinator retains its original server objects.
findings.impact: The settings screen can show a secure configuration while an already-running live poller still uses the previous transport until restart.
findings.fix: Include every supported transport/certificate field in lifecycle decisions, or resolve and apply current connection policy atomically on every operation.
accept: An FTPS-only change affects the next live, XML and detail operation.
HTTPS-only and certificate-policy-only changes are applied consistently.
Invalid certificates fail without downgrade; validate with an isolated real TLS server.

findings.title: The new hydration hook still keeps stale detail and can skip a new save
findings.kind: Reproduced with the actual hook and a simulated hook lifecycle
findings.detail: With the same save/farm/pen key, replacing the source generation did not re-fetch detail: health stayed 60 instead of 90. Switching A to B with the same pen ID cleared state in one effect, but the next effect read the old hydratedRef and skipped B's request. The fixture ended with an unhydrated B row and no B fetch.
findings.impact: Summaries can stop following current animal detail, or lose detail after a save/farm switch despite the initial snapshot now looking correct. The hook simulation is not an end-to-end Preact/browser race test.
findings.fix: Key hydration by save, farm, pen and source generation; reset the cache/ref atomically and keep request identity explicit. Do not let a prior-context cache suppress a new-context fetch.
accept: Same-save generation changes refresh already-hydrated pens.
A-to-B switching with equal pen IDs fetches B and never displays or uses A detail as B.
A-to-B-to-A, empty pens, failures/retry and unmounts pass under real Preact scheduling and deferred network responses.

findings.title: The new pasture summary tests exercise a copy of production logic
findings.kind: Direct review of the new test file
findings.detail: `pastureStockSummary.test.js` defines its own summarizePastureAnimals function and asserts that copy. It does not import the production TypeScript function.
findings.impact: The tests can remain green when the real parser regresses or is changed independently, leaving the visible remediation unprotected.
findings.fix: Test the actual exported production helper through the TypeScript test toolchain, and add a rendered summary/detail regression using the same fixture.
accept: Changing the production summary arithmetic causes the test to fail.
Measured zero, unknown health, unknown sex, weighted cluster counts and empty pens are exercised through production code.
A frozen BigSky-style snapshot agrees across overview, pasture summary and animal table.

findings.title: Classic-to-RF import drops secure transport policy
findings.kind: Reproduced against the new edition-policy helper
findings.detail: The import allowlist correctly removes passwords and feed codes, but also omits ftpSecure, FTP TLS policy and httpFeedSecure. The fixture imported a secure server with neither secure flag. The packaged FTP helper defaults an unspecified transport to plaintext.
findings.impact: After the user re-enters credentials, an imported connection can downgrade when the server accepts plaintext, or fail unexpectedly when it requires TLS.
findings.fix: Preserve validated non-secret transport settings during import, or import the connection disabled with an explicit transport confirmation. Continue excluding all secrets and LAN exposure settings.
accept: Import explicit FTPS and HTTPS feed configurations without copying credentials.
Re-entering credentials retains the original secure transport and certificate policy.
Unknown or obsolete transport values require a visible decision, never silent plaintext fallback.

findings.title: IPC hardening covers launch, not the privileged bridge as a whole
findings.kind: Source and URL-helper fixtures; exploit reachability remains conditional
findings.detail: The new URL helper accepts arbitrary file:///.../index.html and setup.html paths. Sender checking uses webContents.getURL rather than senderFrame identity. The candidate still exposes configuration and LAN handlers without per-handler sender validation, while navigation accepts arbitrary file URLs.
findings.impact: An untrusted document or frame reaching the preload bridge would have more authority than intended. No such hostile-document entry path was established in this audit.
findings.fix: Centralize privileged IPC authorization using the known window/webContents, trusted main frame, exact packaged paths and exact loopback scheme/effective port. Apply it to reads containing secrets as well as writes.
accept: Reject outside files named index.html or setup.html, unexpected windows and child frames.
Reject default-port localhost URLs when the application uses 8766/8768.
Prove every privileged bridge handler invokes the shared guard; test permitted setup/dashboard flows too.

findings.title: Early image-export failures still ignore dialog suppression
findings.kind: Candidate-source confirmation
findings.detail: The unsupported-platform and missing-script exits call native dialogs directly despite suppressNative being available. Later errors use the shared presentation path.
findings.impact: A browser/UI-triggered failure can unexpectedly open a native desktop dialog instead of remaining in its requesting surface.
findings.fix: Send all early and late export errors through the same presentation policy and return a structured result.
accept: Every early failure with suppressNative:true opens no native dialog.
The desktop invocation still presents an intentional dialog when suppression is false.

prior.title: A late bootstrap response can still display one save under another save's name
prior.evidence: Previous evidence retained; no sufficient current closure test in this pass
prior.note: Do not interpret the green generic suites as closure. Repeat the specific prior regression against the intended current build.
prior.accept: Delay initial A beyond splash dismissal, switch to B and complete B then A. B must remain selected with B's payload. Cover bootstrap, manual refresh, fallback polling and WS overlap.
prior.fix: Capture the request's server ID and context generation before awaiting, then validate both before ingestion, including startup. Apply one identity-aware ingestion contract to every source.

prior.title: Nonthrowing I/O failures can still be reported as successful export replacement
prior.evidence: Confirmed in the newly packaged RF mod source; no game fault injection
prior.note: The copy wrapper discards copyFile's result and accepts a nonthrowing call plus an existing destination. Move recovery can then delete the source. Atomic/direct/mirror write paths do not consistently check write and close outcomes; saveFile fallback equates pcall success with persisted success.
prior.accept: Fault-inject false-return copy/write/close/save operations, including an existing destination. Previous bytes remain usable, no success notification is emitted and a later valid retry recovers.
prior.fix: Define one successful replacement contract across rename, copy, write, close, save and mirror paths. Preserve previous good bytes and the recoverable source on failure; advance success/generation bookkeeping only after confirmed replacement.

prior.title: Opaque browser origins still receive loopback trust
prior.evidence: Reproduced in isolated candidate-code fixtures
prior.note: `getRequestOrigin` turns explicit Origin: null and malformed origins into an empty string. Both the write guard and WebSocket origin guard then take the no-origin local-client branch. The fixture accepted both, while rejecting an ordinary hostile HTTPS origin.
prior.accept: Hostile, malformed and explicit null origins fail for WS, livestock requests and export. Authorized native/desktop clients continue to work.
prior.fix: Distinguish an absent Origin from an invalid or opaque one; reject explicit null/malformed origins. Require scoped authorization for sensitive browser operations rather than granting it from locality alone.

prior.title: FTP detail listing filenames can escape the Windows cache root
prior.evidence: Reproduced in an isolated Windows-path fixture
prior.note: `syncFtpDetailsCache` only checks that a remote entry starts with animals_ and ends with .json. Backslashes and traversal components survive into path.join. A mocked listing directed the download to C:\audit\outside.json instead of the userData subtree.
prior.accept: Malicious MLSD/Unix listing entries never initiate outside-root writes. Legitimate integer and composite animal filenames continue to sync.
prior.fix: Validate the complete allowed filename grammar, reject both separator types and enforce resolved containment against a fixed trusted root immediately before temporary download and final rename.

prior.title: The new focus trap moves password typing back into the username field
prior.evidence: Previous evidence retained; no sufficient current closure test in this pass
prior.note: Do not interpret the green generic suites as closure. Repeat the specific prior regression against the intended current build.
prior.accept: Type an entire username/password normally without focus moving unexpectedly; changing input state or delivering a live payload must not reset focus. Escape and focus restoration must still work.
prior.fix: Keep the Escape callback in a ref or stabilize it, and attach initial-focus/trap lifecycle only when the dialog actually opens. Add background inertness and proper stacked-dialog ownership.

prior.title: Concurrent requests for the same save can overwrite newer data with older data
prior.evidence: Previous evidence retained; no sufficient current closure test in this pass
prior.note: Do not interpret the green generic suites as closure. Repeat the specific prior regression against the intended current build.
prior.accept: Reverse same-save HTTP completion and interleave HTTP with newer WS revisions. The displayed source revision never decreases.
prior.fix: Reject older source revisions and sequence responses within a context, or serialize/coalesce duplicate requests. Identity checks alone do not establish freshness.

prior.title: An authoritative zero herd size still preserves nonzero cluster rows
prior.evidence: Previous evidence retained; no sufficient current closure test in this pass
prior.note: Do not interpret the green generic suites as closure. Repeat the specific prior regression against the intended current build.
prior.accept: For targets0,1,5 and larger values, emitted counts sum to the authoritative target before any explicit display cap. Missing totals must follow a different documented fallback.
prior.fix: Distinguish missing/nonfinite totals from valid zero. A successful authoritative0 must produce an empty or zero-count result; coordinate with backend section-success semantics.

prior.title: The display formatter still turns a zero-health synthetic animal into100%
prior.evidence: Previous evidence retained; no sufficient current closure test in this pass
prior.note: Do not interpret the green generic suites as closure. Repeat the specific prior regression against the intended current build.
prior.accept: A synthetic zero-health row renders0% with the appropriate warning; a genuinely unknown reading is identified as unknown or explicitly estimated, never silently healthy.
prior.fix: Preserve finite zero in every presentation/alert helper and represent missing sample health separately from a measured zero. Test the rendered consumer, not only the producer.

prior.title: Population correction changes counts without reconciling the statistics they divide
prior.evidence: Packaged-mod source confirmation
prior.note: Sampled buckets scale count and weighted sums together, then correct count alone to meet the reported population. Later averages divide unchanged sums by corrected counts. The inspected average helper also drops nonpositive sums, so measured all-zero health does not become an explicit aggregate zero.
prior.accept: Uniform-population samples preserve their averages after up/down correction. Every category total is between0 and the corresponding population, and all buckets reconcile to the authoritative total.
prior.fix: Reconcile counts, weighted sums and categorical totals under one sampling/allocation contract, preserving sample means and disclosing estimates.

prior.title: The cached finance path still falls back to purchase price instead of resale value
prior.evidence: Packaged-mod source confirmation
prior.note: The incremental-fleet finance branch reads row.sellValue, row.sellPrice or row.price. The inspected vehicle serializer writes purchase price into row.price and the shown sell-value path stores it under ads.sellValue.
prior.accept: The same depreciated fleet and farm scope produces equivalent asset valuation with Courseplay enabled or disabled, including owned, leased and unknown-owner rows.
prior.fix: Export and consume a canonical resale-value field and one ownership scope across both finance paths; do not silently replace resale with purchase price.

prior.title: The remaining Courseplay shield still traverses the full fleet twice per update
prior.evidence: Packaged-mod source confirmation; no FPS benchmark
prior.note: FarmDashboard:update calls the compatibility tick. When Courseplay is loaded, shieldFleetIfNeeded performs two complete fleet passes on each tick, without the no-Courseplay pending-work gate.
prior.accept: Instrument examined vehicles across an unchanged fleet and newly loaded vehicles. Idle updates perform no recurring full scans while newly eligible vehicles still receive protection.
prior.fix: Use a bounded change-driven queue or registration lifecycle and avoid rescanning unchanged vehicles on every update.

prior.title: Runtime cadence changes do not update the adaptive scheduler's requested-value cache
prior.evidence: Packaged-mod source confirmation
prior.note: _userCollectionCycleMs is captured during config load and preferred by adaptive cadence. The inspected synced-settings and setInt paths update config.collectionCycleMs but not that requested-value field.
prior.accept: Increase and decrease cadence through local and synchronized settings, trigger adaptive probes and save/reload. The requested preference is never overwritten by an obsolete cached value.
prior.fix: Maintain one canonical requested cadence and update it through every local, synchronized, load and save entry point; keep effective/adaptive cadence separate.

prior.title: Coroutine and legacy collector failures still look like successful fresh collection
prior.evidence: Packaged-mod source confirmation; full scheduler fault injection outstanding
prior.note: `safeCollect` returns an empty table both for missing/failed collection and for empty results, without an error status. Legacy collection consumes that result, and other completion paths still update cached data/finish slices without a uniform failure envelope.
prior.accept: Inject a failure into each supported collector mode. Failed sections are marked failed/stale; successful emptiness still clears old data and does not trigger failure fallback.
prior.fix: Propagate explicit success, failure, generation and last-success time through every collection mode. Keep stale fallback data with an honest status instead of converting failure to empty success.

prior.title: Station-name guesses still generate unverified selling offers
prior.evidence: Packaged-mod source confirmation
prior.note: Although synthetic whole stations were removed, Method 8 still inserts products and fixed multipliers into existing named stations, including Grain Mill and Biogas Plant. Those prices feed the crop min/max/best-location calculation.
prior.accept: A wheat-only mill never receives a soybean offer through name matching. Every actionable destination/product/price pair corresponds to an actual station offer.
prior.fix: Read product acceptance and prices from real station data. If estimates are retained, place them in a clearly separate non-actionable estimate model.

prior.title: Bale scanning charges accepted entries rather than all traversal work
prior.evidence: Packaged-mod source confirmation
prior.note: The iterator restarts pairs over a source table, skips previously seen entries, and increments its cap primarily for newly accepted entries. A large table of non-bale or already-seen objects can therefore require a broad scan in one slice.
prior.accept: Instrument examined entries on large eligible/ineligible tables. Every slice stays within its work budget and final output is complete and deduplicated.
prior.fix: Retain mutation-safe enumeration state across slices and charge every examined entry, independently of whether it becomes an exported bale.

prior.title: Pollers still overlap and stale work can overwrite replacement server state
prior.evidence: Candidate-source confirmation of the overlapping FTP branch
prior.note: The interval starts another batch without awaiting the previous batch. Poll generation checks occur before safeDownload and after it, but safeDownload replaces the final file internally before the post-download generation check. Generation-specific temporary names do not prevent an older operation from committing the shared final file.
prior.accept: Slow cycles never overlap. Old completions cannot mutate replacement state. Repeated watcher failures leave exactly one live scheduler and no orphan debounce.
prior.fix: Serialize/coalesce per-server work; use configuration generations and cancellation; dispose every timer; validate identity after awaits and before filesystem commits or state mutation.

prior.title: An active HTTP response can outlive the advertised total deadline
prior.evidence: Reproduced with candidate code and a simulated trickle response
prior.note: The 45-second deadline is checked when entering a request/redirect, but there is no independent wall-clock cancellation timer for an active body. A mocked stream was still pending at 60 seconds and then returned HTTP 200. Response aborted/error settlement also remains incomplete in the inspected function.
prior.accept: Trickle, stalled, aborted and truncated fixtures terminate within the total deadline. Valid bounded redirects and normal responses still succeed.
prior.fix: Use an independent total-deadline timer; destroy outstanding requests/responses on settlement; handle response failures and propagate cancellation across redirects.

prior.title: Detail caches can still remain stale when indexes or clocks are unreliable
prior.evidence: Candidate-source confirmation
prior.note: Bulk detail sync compares remote mtime with the downloaded file's local mtime. Per-pen detail re-fetches only when dirtyAt is positive and newer than the local timestamp; a cached file with a missing index can therefore be reused indefinitely.
prior.accept: Equal-length changes are visible; missing-index data refreshes within a documented interval; source/client clock offsets do not prevent updates.
prior.fix: Persist remote generation/mtime/hash independently of local file time, add bounded fallback refresh without an index and define per-pen versus bulk precedence.

prior.title: Unstamped exports regain freshness on restart and omit some generation changes
prior.evidence: Candidate-source confirmation of the accepted unstamped-export path
prior.note: The content hash excludes weather and is not included in the persisted cache identity. On new in-memory state, the same unstamped export receives a new receipt-based lastLuaReceivedAt.
prior.accept: Restart/retrieval preserves the age of identical unstamped exports. A genuinely new source generation restores freshness even when ordinary farm values do not change.
prior.fix: Persist source-generation identity and age and distinguish collection time from receipt. Align exporter field/type and backend parsing, with an explicit fallback contract for older exports.

prior.title: Hold and last-good helpers can resurrect cleared animals, stock and RF data
prior.evidence: Candidate-source confirmation
prior.note: Backup updates remember nonempty animals without clearing the prior backup on an authoritative empty result. Snapshot forwarding restores previous animals/stock when the next section is empty; stock and RF hold branches still conflate empty with unavailable.
prior.accept: Exercise populated-to-empty animals and stock, RF disable, persistence and restart end-to-end. Successful emptiness remains empty; a genuine collection failure retains only clearly stale fallback data.
prior.fix: Carry explicit successful-empty/disabled versus failed/omitted section status and generation through merge, hold, backups and persistence. Clear every corresponding backup on an authoritative clear.

prior.title: Detail generation is dropped before comparison and stale animals attach to zero-count pens
prior.evidence: Reproduced in isolated candidate-helper fixtures
prior.note: `makeCacheEntry` still drops generatedAt. A husbandry reporting zero animals accepted two retained detail rows and was marked hydrated. The newer code prefers some smaller unique-ID lists, but does not establish generation correctness or a zero-population tombstone.
prior.accept: Both enumeration orders select the newest compatible generation. A zero pen has no stale individuals, and genuine empty detail is a valid result rather than a reason to resurrect older rows.
prior.fix: Preserve and validate detail generation plus world/pen identity. Invalidate incompatible individuals on authoritative zero and handle successful empty detail explicitly.

prior.title: Unresolved vehicle ownership is still inferred from unrelated farm characteristics
prior.evidence: Candidate-source confirmation
prior.note: The transient-pool resolver scores farms using livestock, land, current fleet and ADS presence, then writes the selected farm into ownerFarmId/farmId when the fallback applies.
prior.accept: For ambiguous records, changing livestock, field or fleet counts does not change ownership. Only authoritative matching evidence assigns an owner.
prior.fix: Require authoritative identity/ownership matches or retain an explicit unresolved pool. Do not convert a heuristic ranking into exact ownership.

prior.title: Configuration and UID indexes can reuse the same saved vehicle for two live records
prior.evidence: Reproduced using the candidate matching branches
prior.note: A configuration-key match removes a row from one list but leaves its UID index available. The fixture matched the same XML object first by configuration and then again by UID.
prior.accept: Mixed configuration/UID matches in either order remain one-to-one. A consumed saved record can never enrich a second live vehicle.
prior.fix: Use a global consumed-record set checked by every matching index, with one canonical identity for each saved record.

prior.title: Saved ownership still wins and field/farmland ID collisions drop live-only fields
prior.evidence: Candidate-source confirmation of one remaining branch
prior.note: The Lua-only append branch checks seenKeys against both field.id and farmlandId even though XML keys use farmlandId-or-id. A valid field can be suppressed because its field ID happens to equal a different record's farmland ID. The separate prior ownership-precedence branch was not fully re-executed here.
prior.accept: Test transfer, relinquishment, added fields and overlapping field/farmland numbers. Live ownership and all distinct valid fields survive merging.
prior.fix: Preserve authoritative live ownership including valid zero and use typed canonical field/farmland identities. Distinguish absence from explicit unowned state.

prior.title: Aggregate XML fingerprints still collide for masked optional-file changes
prior.evidence: Reproduced with a synthetic per-file stat fixture
prior.note: The fingerprint remains maximum mtime plus total size. Changing one file's mtime from 1000 to 2000 while another remained 9999 produced the same fingerprint, 9999:200.
prior.accept: Same-size optional rewrites with preserved/masked timestamps and optional-file creation/deletion produce a changed fingerprint; unchanged inputs remain stable.
prior.fix: Fingerprint each input's name, existence and metadata or content, rather than only aggregate maxima and sums.

prior.title: The Lua syntax check cannot start after the dependency refresh
prior.evidence: Reproduced by the requested validation command
prior.note: `node tools/check-lua-syntax.mjs` exits with MODULE_NOT_FOUND for luaparse. No Lua files were parsed by this attempted gate.
prior.accept: A clean dependency install can run the checker over all shipped Lua files and reports real parse results; the gate fails CI on a deliberate syntax fixture.
prior.fix: Declare/pin the checker dependency in the owning tooling package, handle the BOM policy explicitly and wire the mod syntax check into CI. Do not mistake tool startup failure for a game syntax failure.

prior.title: The ownership integration test returns successfully when its expected result is absent
prior.evidence: Observed in the current Jest output
prior.note: The transient-pool integration case returned early when the expected remapped vehicle was absent. The live Giants HTTP-feed case returned early unless its opt-in environment was set. Jest counted both as passes.
prior.accept: Deliberately break remapping or expected ownership and this test fails. Missing optional live prerequisites are reported as skipped, while the hermetic equivalent always executes.
prior.fix: Use hermetic committed fixtures, exact owner assertions and assertion-count enforcement. Make unavoidable environment-dependent skips explicit before execution, never contingent on the expected result being missing.

prior.title: Raw map identifiers still select overview images outside the source root
prior.evidence: Previous evidence retained; no sufficient current closure test in this pass
prior.note: Do not interpret the green generic suites as closure. Repeat the specific prior regression against the intended current build.
prior.accept: Outside overview fixtures cannot be selected or returned; legitimate custom map exports still resolve.
prior.fix: Validate the raw lookup key and enforce source-root containment before opening or copying files, independently of output filename normalization.

prior.title: Transport-only saves can leave the live poller on plaintext FTP
prior.evidence: Reproduced in configuration fixtures; retained poller object confirmed in candidate source
prior.note: The server signature includes connection identity and secret revisions but omits ftpSecure and httpFeedSecure. Changing only either flag returns no reboot. The FTP coordinator retains its original server objects.
prior.accept: A transport-only save changes the next operation on every FTP path. Invalid certificates fail closed. UI status reflects the active transport and any explicit legacy choice.
prior.fix: Include every connection-policy field in lifecycle decisions or resolve current configuration each cycle. Make legacy plaintext an explicit informed choice, without silent downgrade.

prior.title: HTTP discovery errors are treated as a successful empty server list
prior.evidence: Previous evidence retained; no sufficient current closure test in this pass
prior.note: Do not interpret the green generic suites as closure. Repeat the specific prior regression against the intended current build.
prior.accept: First discovery returns503, then200 with saves. The UI recovers the save selector without reloading;401 triggers authentication rather than an empty configuration.
prior.fix: Throw a structured status-aware discovery error, distinguish genuine zero configurations from failed discovery and let the complete startup retry restore the server list.

prior.title: Failed settings hydration still enables saving unloaded defaults
prior.evidence: Previous evidence retained; no sufficient current closure test in this pass
prior.note: Do not interpret the green generic suites as closure. Repeat the specific prior regression against the intended current build.
prior.accept: Fail each load stage and ensure unloaded sections cannot be persisted. Fail each save stage and display exact committed/failed sections without a generic saved/synced claim.
prior.fix: Track successful hydration per editable section, block writes to unknown values, validate before any commit and report explicit per-section partial outcomes. Keep drafts and a retry path.

prior.title: Authentication still proceeds on timeout and clears valid credentials on network failure
prior.evidence: Previous evidence retained; no sufficient current closure test in this pass
prior.note: Do not interpret the green generic suites as closure. Repeat the specific prior regression against the intended current build.
prior.accept: Cover early completion, >30s login, hung network,401, temporary outage and double-submit. No protected bootstrap occurs before authorization and saved credentials survive transport errors.
prior.fix: Use one persistent authentication state and in-flight verification promise, explicit deadlines and separate rejected/network states. Only successful authorization releases protected startup, and transport failure must not erase valid credentials.

prior.title: SimHub waits for authentication before mounting the component that performs it
prior.evidence: Previous evidence retained; no sufficient current closure test in this pass
prior.note: Do not interpret the green generic suites as closure. Repeat the specific prior regression against the intended current build.
prior.accept: A direct unauthenticated SimHub URL shows login immediately; cached authorization verifies without the artificial30s delay;401/403/503/non-JSON responses have clear recoverable states.
prior.fix: Mount the auth/bootstrap boundary independently of readiness, release data loading on successful authentication and handle status before parsing response bodies.

prior.title: A missing Windows save path is still described as rejected credentials
prior.evidence: Previous evidence retained; no sufficient current closure test in this pass
prior.note: Do not interpret the green generic suites as closure. Repeat the specific prior regression against the intended current build.
prior.accept: ENOENT/ENOTDIR paths under C:\Users map to path errors;EACCES maps to permissions;real401/403/auth rejection remains authentication-specific.
prior.fix: Preserve explicit error codes and classify OS error identifiers before incidental message words or path text. Keep fallback text matching narrow.

prior.title: Early image-export failures ignore native-dialog suppression
prior.evidence: Candidate-source confirmation
prior.note: The unsupported-platform and missing-script exits call native dialogs directly despite suppressNative being available. Later errors use the shared presentation path.
prior.accept: All early failures honor suppressNative:true and return the expected structured error without native dialogs.
prior.fix: Route every early and late failure through one presentation policy and return structured errors to the requesting UI.

remediation.title: Close trust and persistence blockers
steps: Centralize request-origin and IPC authorization and cover the entire route/bridge surface, not only the new launch handler.
Validate FTP filenames and contained destinations before any filesystem action; use one shared safe path contract.
Implement last-good-preserving replacement with explicit copy/write/close success for desktop and mod paths.
Turn the isolated counterexamples into production-linked failing regression tests, then close them before rebuilding.
remediation.gate: No opaque-origin or cache-escape acceptance; failed replacement preserves original bytes; privileged sender tests pass.

remediation.title: Make data identity and clears authoritative
steps: Define save/farm/source-generation identity and propagate it from collection through disk, merge, HTTP/WS and hydration.
Fix zero/empty/omitted/failed semantics and persist generation-scoped clears.
Make detail hydration refreshable and context-safe; use one-to-one entity matching and separate field/farmland indices.
Replace aggregate metadata fingerprints with per-file identities and bound missing-index revalidation.
Run real Preact deferred-response cases as well as backend fixtures.
remediation.gate: No stale generation or old animal can reappear after clear, switch, refresh or restart; no XML entity is consumed twice.

remediation.title: Finish transport and efficiency lifecycle
steps: Preserve secure non-secret connection policy in import and apply policy changes to every active transfer path.
Serialize per-server polls and recheck cancellation immediately before commit.
Use an absolute HTTP deadline with complete abort/error cleanup.
Gate Courseplay repair work on pending transitions and budget every inspected inventory entry.
Profile iteration counts and slice durations with realistic large herds/fleets instead of relying on nominal caps.
remediation.gate: No silent transport downgrade, overlapping per-context commits or unbounded trickle requests; large-save slice budgets are measured.

remediation.title: Finish domain truth and end-user recovery
steps: Separate sample means from population estimates and preserve known zero values.
Use canonical vehicle valuation and real sell-station offers.
Propagate collection failure explicitly rather than empty success.
Repeat the outstanding auth, SimHub, failed-settings hydration, startup race and error-classification regressions.
Polish contrast, source-age language, long labels and below-fold livestock navigation without reintroducing generic redesign churn.
remediation.gate: Frozen snapshot parity plus failure-mode usability passes across dashboard, detail, setup, settings and read-only viewers.

remediation.title: Make validation enforce the real implementation
steps: Make the Lua parser reproducibly available and run the declared syntax gate against all intended files.
Replace copied summary tests with production imports and use deterministic ownership fixtures.
Report genuine skips separately; make missing required fixture records fail.
Add unique private build identity, rebuild only to a fresh private directory and capture hashes/versions/feed mapping.
Run the automated suite from a clean dependency installation.
remediation.gate: Reproducible production-linked tests; no vacuous integration passes; Lua gate succeeds; intended artifacts are uniquely identifiable.

remediation.title: Run safe installed acceptance, then approve a private handoff
steps: Obtain action-time approval for installer execution; use disposable profiles for destructive migration/uninstall cases.
Install the approved Classic/RF pair and verify both windows, ports and independent profiles concurrently.
Walk unchanged setup, selected-save return, dashboard/pasture/detail agreement and failure recovery.
During an agreed safe game window, verify Classic mod 3.4.0.8 and RF mod 5.0.0.1 pairings without overwriting the active save.
Exercise a real dedicated connection, reconnect, stale-detail recovery and bounded soak; a mirror snapshot is not a live dedicated pass.
Only after gates pass, prepare an approved private tester packet. Keep public 4.2.1 and its update story untouched.
remediation.gate: Signed-off installed and live evidence is attached to exact hashes; public channel files are unchanged.

conditional.title: Proxy and Host trust still require an explicit deployment policy
conditional.detail: Setup rejects an unrecognized public Host, but general API authorization still trusts loopback independently of Host. A reverse proxy that rewrites Host to localhost can inherit local/setup trust.
conditional.boundary: No public proxy deployment or DNS-rebinding exploit was established.
conditional.fix: Define trusted-proxy behavior and require appropriate authentication beyond network locality. Exercise preserved and rewritten Host cases before exposing the service.

conditional.title: Navigation allowlists and privileged IPC are not yet tied to exact trusted documents
conditional.detail: Navigation/window guards now exist, but allow arbitrary file: URLs and accept default-port localhost URLs through u.port || PORT. Privileged IPC handlers still omit sender/frame validation. A fixture accepted an outside file document and localhost:80 while rejecting external HTTPS.
conditional.boundary: No hostile-document navigation path or renderer exploit was established.
conditional.fix: Match exact schemes, effective ports and packaged file paths; validate sender/frame identity for privileged IPC.

conditional.title: Field fallback collection modes still contain unbounded synchronous scans
conditional.detail: MOD-14's default coroutine and bale prepass now yield. Fallback, _smState and legacy branches still disable or bypass yielding before scanning the world.
conditional.boundary: Practical reachability of these fallback modes in the current supported game configuration was not established. No universal frame-stall claim is made.
conditional.fix: Bound every supported mode or explicitly reject unsupported incremental modes. Document mode selection and instrument per-invocation work.

conditional.title: Freshness-gated cycle tails may delay request polling during persistent collector failure
conditional.detail: The examined cycle tail is freshness-gated and contains request polling and detail rotation. A permanently failing collector could prevent that particular tail from running.
conditional.boundary: Alternative servicing paths were not fully excluded, so end-to-end request starvation is not established and is not included in confirmed finding counts.
conditional.fix: Trace every request-servicing path and inject sustained section failure. Servicing should have an independent bounded cadence if this is the only path.
